column1: # manifest.tsv — the unredaction bench's real-world documents (#1591, bench #1590).
# WHAT IS IN GIT AND WHAT IS NOT
# THIS FILE is tracked: ids, URLs, hashes and the VETTING RECORD.
# The PDFs are not — they land in test-pdfs/unredaction-bench/, gitignored.
# The recovered or published VALUES are not, anywhere, ever. There is no column
# for them and UnredactionBenchManifestTests fails if one is added (#1602).
# Ground truth for tier B lives in a gitignored local file built by hand:
#   test-pdfs/unredaction-bench/ground-truth.local.tsv
# so the repository never republishes text a court or an agency tried to
# withhold, even where a newspaper already has.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated)
#   id            stable slug; also the local filename stem
#   tier          B — the hidden value is already published, so the bench can SCORE
#                 C — public record, no published ground truth; leak CLASS only, never values
#                 D — sensitive-provenance sources under a value-free positional design (#1603)
#   status        vetted   — all three vetting questions answered yes; the script downloads it
#                 excluded — assessed and REJECTED; never downloaded. The reason is the point.
#                 unvetted — recorded so the next reader knows it exists and that NOBODY HAS
#                            LOOKED YET. Not downloaded. This is deliberately distinct from
#                            `excluded`: "we checked and it is fine" must not read the same as
#                            "nobody has checked" (#1591).
#   url           direct PDF URL, no credentials, no paid PACER; RECAP mirror where one exists
#   sha256        64 hex of the exact bytes, or `-` when the row is not `vetted`
#   source        court | agency | foia | sec | press
#   public_basis  why this document is lawfully public
#   truth_url     where the hidden value was PUBLISHED (tier B), or `-`
#   vetting       THE ASSESSMENT, not the verdict. Says what was checked and what was found,
#                 including for `excluded` rows, so a later reader can re-judge it.
# VETTING (all three must be yes for `vetted`)
#   1. tier B: the text under the redaction is already published by a reputable
#      outlet or the court; or tier C: the document is plainly public record.
#   2. Recovery would NOT identify private individuals or victims. This is a
#      hard exclusion and it outranks "but it is already posted somewhere".
#   3. The source's terms permit automated download.
#id
doj-epstein-2025-release
column9: EXCLUDED, and not because it is unavailable — it is posted and the files are exactly the failure modes this bench measures. Vetting question 2 fails: the redactions in this release cover victim and third-party names, so recovering them would identify the people the redaction exists to protect, and a bench that scores that recovery is doing the harm regardless of who reads the number. Question 1 also fails for tier B (no published ground truth) and the whole point of the release is that there is none. If this is ever revisited it is under #1603's value-free POSITIONAL design only — measure whether a mark leaks, never what it leaks — and that is a separate decision a human makes, not a status change here.
